adjudications.justification: signatures.md L42-L43 is the Architecture lead-in ('UCP uses HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421) for all HTTP-based transports') — a mechanism statement with no keyword. The MUST is inferred from the section's operative requirements (the Signing requests / Verification MUSTs, SIG-010..SIG-018, SIG-036..SIG-038) which all presuppose RFC 9421 as the only signature mechanism; a non-RFC-9421 signature cannot verify, so the choice is itself observable and is already graded by both lanes (merchant CHECK at 2026-04-08, agent verifier). Kept MUST (decision 29); not a downgrade candidate.

signatures.md L226 is step 3 of the numbered Key Rotation procedure under the lead-in 'To rotate keys without service interruption:' (no keyword). The floor '(minimum 7 days)' is stated as a requirement of the interruption-free procedure; MUST inferred because a verifier that drops an old key earlier than the floor fails signatures the procedure guarantees will verify. Kept MUST for D1-15/D3-23; flagged as a D2-11b downgrade candidate (procedural guidance) — needs-receiver either way.

shopping/catalog/index.md L376 (Common Scenarios / Empty Search): 'When search finds no matches, return an empty array without messages.' — an imperative sentence with no keyword. MUST inferred from the imperative mood in a normative section and from CAT-020's envelope rule (application outcomes return HTTP 200 with the UCP envelope); an implementation that returns an error message for an empty search contradicts the stated behaviour. Kept MUST (decision 29).

shopping/catalog/rest.md L479-L482 (Product Not Found): 'the server returns HTTP 200 with ucp.status: "error" and a descriptive message. This is an application outcome, not a transport error' — descriptive present tense, no keyword. MUST inferred: the sentence defines the only conforming response to an unresolvable identifier (HTTP 200 + error envelope, never a 404), consistent with CAT-020. Kept MUST (decision 29).

shopping/extensions/discount.md L140: the first item of the `**Response behavior:**` list (lead-in at L138; the siblings at L141 and L142 are DSC-007 and DSC-008). NOT `bullet`: that class is 'a list item under a keyword lead-in', and no RFC 2119 keyword appears in the lead-in or in any item of this list (L140 to L142), nor in the `**Request behavior:**` list above it (lead-in L132, items L134 to L136); the nearest keyword is the MUST at L145, which belongs to the separate `**Cart-to-checkout continuity:**` paragraph and states a different requirement. `inferred`: the list states the response contract of the discount extension in definitional present tense, and the same document fixes `discounts.applied` as the array in which discounts are reported (L83, 'The `applied` array explains how discounts were calculated and distributed'; L189, automatic discounts 'Appear in `discounts.applied` with `automatic: true` and no `code` field'), so a response that leaves an active discount out of `applied` misreports the priced cart to a conformant Platform. Kept MUST (decision 29). Relabelled from `bullet` on 2026-09-22 (owner approved, from the adversarial sample review of this batch): `bullet` needs no sign-off while `inferred` is a REVIEW_BASIS, so the earlier label routed the row around the control decision 29 exists to impose.
